modules.module_title: Prepare for carrying out turning operations

pcs.pc_description: check the calibration date of all the measuring equipment to ensure it has not expired

determine the job specifications/ machining requirements by referring to the valid and approved documents, such as job card, operational drawings, approved sketches/illustrations, work drawings, assembly drawings, etc.
extract the relevant information such as tapping sizes and threads; feeds and speeds; component ratings; machining symbols and tolerances from reference charts, tables, graphs
check the process sheet and match it with the received drawings and other specifications
select the appropriate tools, equipment and measuring instruments to be used during the turning operations, and check them to ensure they are not worn out or damaged
check the availability of the required raw material for carrying out turning operations

check the raw material/ components to be machined to ensure they are free from foreign objects, dirt and contamination and have the recommended surface texture, limits and tolerances according to the process sheet
check the post-machining sheet to determine if the component meets the applicable quality standards from the previous machining operations
prepare the work area for turning operations, ensuring there are no hazards in the area
plan to carry out the required turning activities and the sequence of operations as per the specifications
follow the recommended safe working practices
check the runout of chuck and the taper of the tailstock
coordinate with the machine setter to check the machine is ready for use

prepare for carrying out turning operations by mounting, positioning and setting a range of work holding devices and cutting tools, such as chuck, faceplate, centre drills, twist/core drills, reamers, etc.
position and secure the work holding devices to the machine spindle
secure the workpiece/ component in a chuck or work holding device using the appropriate fixture, ensuring no distortion
set the machine tool speeds and feeds to achieve the given component specifications
operate the machine tool controls safely as per the manufacturer’s instructions, both in hand and power modes
identify abnormal noises coming from the machine and component, and adjust the feed and Revolutions Per Minute (RPM), as required
check the condition of the tools being used and repair them, as required
follow the recommended process to stop and restart the turning machine during emergencies

check the geometrical accuracies of components, such as diameter on multiple points, taper, surface finishing, groove depth and width, drill depth, Outer Diameter (OD)/Inner Diameter (ID), threading quality and dimensions
check for the permitted grinding margin on OD/ID

use lathes and other relevant accessories such as the saddle, capstan/turret head, compound slide, tailstock, taper turning attachments, profile attachments, fixed and travelling steadies, as per the requirement

carry out turning operations using the relevant equipment, such as solid high-speed tooling, brazed tip tooling, interchangeable tipped tooling to produce components with various features, such as surface texture and finish, breadth, width, length, etc.
follow the recommended practices to overcome the effects of backlash in machine slides and screws
carry out roughing and finishing appropriately to achieve the required surface finish and dimensional accuracy
follow the recommended practices to minimise tool wear
use the appropriate cutting fluids for different types of materials, such as steel, stainless steel, aluminium, aluminium alloys, copper/copper alloys, cast iron, etc.

check the diameter, parallelism, surface finish, length, width, concentricity and other critical parameters of the machined components using a range of relevant equipment, such as micrometre, Vernier/digital/dial calliper, dial test indicators (DTI), etc.
ensure the machined components are free from false tool cuts, burrs and sharp edges
check the dimensional accuracy by taking a trial cut
perform the relevant quality checks using the appropriate equipment on the machined components before removing them from the machine
record the measured values as per the organisational standards and complete the post- machining inspection sheet
identify inconsistencies in dimensions due to tool wear and correct the offsets accordingly
adjust various machine settings to maintain the desired accuracy as per the operational requirements
identify the worn-out and damaged tools and equipment
sharpen or replace the worn-out/ damaged tools, using the necessary equipment, and modify tool offsets according to the new tools
use the relevant Industry 4.0 manufacturing technologies to ensure interconnectivity, automation, machine learning, and real-time data collection and analysis
follow the relevant safety guidelines while sharpening/ replacing the worn-out/damaged tools
coordinate with the supervisor or other relevant personnel to resolve any complex issues encountered with the turning operations
isolate the turning machine safely after use
carry out regular maintenance of the machine after use, such as cleaning and oiling
collect and dispose of the industrial waste appropriately as per the applicable environmental regulations and organisational procedures
carry out necessary documentation as per the organisational procedure on the completion of machining operations
ensure compliance with the applicable quality standards
optimise the usage of electricity and other resources in various tasks and processes
connect the electrical tools and equipment safely, and turn them off when not in use
